Noms is a British Royal Navy card game tradition, also known as 'Small Ships Rules.' It represents the naval variant of Nomination Whist, distinct from other games using the same name. The secret partnership mechanic and no-shuffle rule reflect the unique conditions of shipboard play.
4 players. Partnerships are secret and determined by card nomination.
13 cards each, dealt in packets (4-3 pattern rotating). Cards are NOT shuffled between handsâ€”only cut.

items.text: Alternative deal pattern: Some players deal 5-3-5 instead of 4-3-3-3; when passed out, same dealer redeals after stacking.
Lower minimum bid: Bidding may start at 7 or 8; some play that if first three pass, fourth is forced to bid 7.
Opponent trick scoring: Each opponent scores one point per trick taken individually, whether the bid succeeds or not.
Misère ranking variant: Misère ranks between 10 and 11; no Mis a Vis. Failed Misère: bidder deducts 10 plus 1 per trick taken; opponents score nothing.
Alternate lead: Player to dealer's left leads to the first trick instead of the bidder.
13 scores 26: A bid of 13 scores 26 points rather than 13.
Slam penalty: If bidder's team wins all tricks having bid less than 13, it counts as failure and opponents score 26.
